name: PulsePoint SomaCycle Sleep Optimizer
body_location: cranial — subdural placement against the anterior hypothalamus, inserted via temporal approach
description:
The SomaCycle implant modulates the hypothalamic sleep-wake circuitry by delivering calibrated low-amplitude electromagnetic pulses that accelerate the transition into slow-wave and REM sleep phases, compress their duration while preserving their restorative depth, and initiate a controlled wake state at the conclusion of a full compressed cycle. A standard biological sleep cycle requiring seven to nine hours is restructured into a four-to-four-and-a-half hour window without loss of cognitive restoration, memory consolidation, or hormonal regulation. The device includes an onboard chronobiological model that adjusts cycle timing based on detected circadian cues — light exposure, core body temperature, and activity history — ensuring that compressed sleep aligns naturally with the user's environment rather than forcing artificial regularity.

The SomaCycle is enormously popular across all working tiers of GLMZ for the simple reason that two to four recovered hours per day is an extraordinary gift in a city where most people work long shifts, commute across stacked transit corridors, and maintain second jobs or family obligations. For a Tier 2 hospital orderly working double shifts, those recovered hours mean seeing their children before bed. For a Tier 3 freelance data analyst, it means the difference between meeting deadlines and burning out. PulsePoint markets the SomaCycle aggressively with the slogan 'Your time, returned' — and it lands, because it is true. The implant has become so common that many employers quietly factor it into scheduling assumptions, which is a source of ongoing labor tension.
installation_requirements: Licensed neurotechnician required; outpatient procedure under local anesthetic and mild sedation; approximately 90-minute installation with 48-hour calibration period post-procedure
maintenance: Firmware sync every six months via any PulsePoint kiosk or compatible clinic terminal; no battery replacement required — harvests thermal energy from normal metabolic function; full recalibration recommended every four years
specifications: {"compressed_sleep_duration": "4.0–4.5 hours", "sleep_stage_accuracy": "98.2% restorative equivalence to natural 8hr cycle", "pulse_frequency": "0.5–2Hz variable, adaptive", "chronobiological_model": "rolling 30-day adaptive baseline", "power_source": "thermoelectric harvest, supplemented by inductive pad (optional)", "device_lifespan": "10 years", "dimensions": "9mm x 6mm ovoid"}
side_effects: Vivid, highly narrative dreams during the first two to three weeks of calibration as REM compression stabilizes
Mild difficulty waking without the device's cue signal if the user attempts to sleep beyond the compressed window
Occasional hypnagogic hallucinations in the first week post-installation, resolving during calibration
Some users report a persistent mild alertness that makes voluntary napping difficult
cultural_context: The SomaCycle sits at a cultural intersection of aspiration and exhaustion in GLMZ. Among Tier 2 and 3 workers, it is a practical necessity dressed up in wellness branding — people get it because they need the hours, not because they are optimizing. PulsePoint's advertising skews toward showing parents at breakfast tables, artists finishing late-night work, students studying — images of reclaimed life rather than productivity metrics. There is a countercultural undercurrent among some Tier 1 communities who distrust the idea of a corporation managing their sleep, and labor advocacy groups have published reports arguing that the SomaCycle's normalization has allowed employers to implicitly extend the working day without additional compensation. Tier 4 and 5 users tend to pair it with more comprehensive circadian suites, viewing the SomaCycle alone as a somewhat basic option.
known_users: shift workers in manufacturing, transit, and healthcare
parents of young children across all working tiers
students at GLMZ's overcrowded public universities
freelance creatives and gig economy workers managing multiple income streams
anyone with a two-hour commute who cannot afford to lose eight hours to sleep
story_hooks: A wave of SomaCycle users in a Tier 1 district are reporting that their compressed sleep is being interrupted at the same moment each night — 3:14 AM — by what feels like a full-body startle reflex. No firmware anomaly is detectable. The interruptions began the same week a new cellular relay tower was installed on the Shelf.

A PulsePoint internal memo leaks suggesting that SomaCycle devices sold through a specific municipal subsidy program were shipped with a secondary data-collection module that logs not just sleep metrics but ambient audio during the sleep window.

A labor arbitration case hinges on whether a Tier 2 logistics company can legally include SomaCycle ownership as an implicit condition of employment — and a player is subpoenaed as a witness because their device logs are the only record of how many hours the plaintiff actually worked.
